'''Lance Allen Liotta''' is an American pathologist, biomedical engineer, and cancer researcher.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Foretek |first1=Jared |title=GMU's COVID-19 research targets frontline health-care worker... |url=https://www.insidenova.com/news/gmus-covid-19-research-targets-frontline-health-care-workers-b2ddf1ddc429 |website=InsideNoVa |language=en |date=25 November 2020}}</ref> He is a university professor and co-director of the Center for Applied Proteomics and Molecular Medicine at [[George Mason University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mason scientists Lance Liotta and Virginia Espina share how their research helps expand on-campus COVID testing – The Institute for Biohealth Innovation |url=https://ibi.gmu.edu/news/mason-scientists-lance-liotta-and-virginia-espina-share-how-their-research-helps-expand-on-campus-covid-testing/ |access-date=2026-11-08 |website=ibi.gmu.edu}}</ref> His research has addressed the mechanisms of [[cancer metastasis]]<ref>{{Cite news |date=2015-11-20 |title=New patent paves way for breast cancer prevention |url=https://medicalxpress.com/news/2015-11-patent-paves-breast-cancer.html |access-date=2026-11-08 |work=Medical Xpress |language=en-US}}</ref>, [[extracellular matrix]] remodeling, molecular analysis of tissue, and technologies for detecting proteins and other disease-associated [[biomarkers]].

== Education and career ==
Liotta received a BA in biology from [[Hiram College]] in 1969, a PhD in biomedical engineering from [[Case Western Reserve University]] in 1974, and an MD from the same institution in 1976. He became board-certified in anatomic pathology in 1980.<ref name="science.gmu.edu-1">{{Cite web |title=Lance Liotta {{!}} GMU College of Science |url=https://science.gmu.edu/directory/lance-liotta |access-date=2026-11-08 |website=science.gmu.edu}}</ref>

He joined the [[National Cancer Institute]] (NCI) in 1976 for pathology residency training and held position as chief of the Section of Tumor Invasion and Metastasis and chief of the Laboratory of Pathology.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-21 |title=Lance A. Liotta, Ph.D., M.D. {{!}} National Institutes of Health (NIH) |url=https://www.nih.gov/about-nih/nih-almanac/lance-liotta-phd-md |access-date=2026-11-08 |website=www.nih.gov |language=en}}</ref> He served as deputy director for intramural research and training at the [[National Institutes of Health]] from 1992 to 1993.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The NIH Catalyst Celebrates 30 Years {{!}} NIH Intramural Research Program |url=https://irp.nih.gov/catalyst/31/2/the-nih-catalyst-celebrates-30-years |access-date=2026-11-08 |website=irp.nih.gov}}</ref> In 2005, he joined [[George Mason University]], where he co-founded the Center for Applied Proteomics and Molecular Medicine with Emanuel Petricoin.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lane A. Liotta |url=https://vasem.org/member/lane-a-liotta/ |access-date=2026-11-08 |website=VASEM |language=en-US}}</ref>
== Research ==

=== Cancer invasion and metastasis ===
Liotta's early research examined the relationship between tumor cells in the circulation, [[Circulatory system|tumor vasculature]], and [[Lung cancer|lung metastasis]]. His studies in 1974 and 1976 investigated the role of circulating [[tumor cells]] and cell aggregates in the formation of [[Metastasis|metastases]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Liotta |first1=L. A. |last2=Kleinerman |first2=J. |last3=Saidel |first3=G. M. |date=1974 |title=Quantitative relationships of intravascular tumor cells, tumor vessels, and pulmonary metastases following tumor implantation |journal=Cancer Research |volume=34 |issue=5 |pages=997–1004 |issn=0008-5472 |pmid=4841969}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Liotta |first1=L. A. |last2=Saidel |first2=M. G. |last3=Kleinerman |first3=J. |date=1976 |title=The significance of hematogenous tumor cell clumps in the metastatic process |journal=Cancer Research |volume=36 |issue=3 |pages=889–894 |issn=0008-5472 |pmid=1253177}}</ref>

Subsequent research linked tumor invasion to the enzymatic degradation of basement-membrane collagen and examined the role of cytokine-induced pseudopodial extension in [[cell migration]]. Liotta described the process of tumor invasion as a sequence of adhesion, degradation, and movement.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Liotta |first1=L. A. |last2=Tryggvason |first2=K. |last3=Garbisa |first3=S. |last4=Hart |first4=I. |last5=Foltz |first5=C. === Extracellular matrix and metalloproteinases ===
In 1979, Liotta and colleagues reported the preferential degradation of basement-membrane collagen by an enzyme isolated from a metastatic mouse tumor, in research related to the later characterization of matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP-2).His other collaborative studies examined the composition of basement membranes and identified tissue inhibitor of [[Metalloproteinase|metalloproteinases 2]] (TIMP-2).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Liotta |first1=L A |last2=Abe |first2=S |last3=Robey |first3=P G |last4=Martin |first4=G R |date=1979 |title=Preferential digestion of basement membrane collagen by an enzyme derived from a metastatic murine tumor. |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=76 |issue=5 |pages=2268–2272 |doi=10.1073/pnas.76.5.2268 |doi-access=free |pmid=221920 |pmc=383580 |bibcode=1979PNAS...76.2268L |issn=0027-8424}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kleinman |first1=Hynda K. |last2=McGarvey |first2=Mary L. |last3=Liotta |first3=Lance A. |last4=Robey |first4=Pamela Gehron |last5=Tryggvason |first5=Karl |last6=Martin |first6=George R. |date=1982-11-01 |title=Isolation and characterization of type IV procollagen, laminin, and heparan sulfate proteoglycan from the EHS sarcoma |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/bi00267a025 |journal=Biochemistry |volume=21 |issue=24 |pages=6188–6193 |doi=10.1021/bi00267a025 |pmid=6217835 |issn=0006-2960}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Stetler-Stevenson |first1=W. G. |last2=Krutzsch |first2=H. C. |last3=Liotta |first3=L. A. |date=1989-10-15 |title=Tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase (TIMP-2). A new member of the metalloproteinase inhibitor family |journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry |volume=264 |issue=29 |pages=17374–17378 |doi=10.1016/S0021-9258(18)71503-2 |doi-access=free |issn=0021-9258 |pmid=2793861}}</ref>

=== Laser capture microdissection ===
Liotta was part of the multidisciplinary team that developed laser capture microdissection, a method for selecting and isolating cells from heterogeneous tissue sections for molecular analysis. The technique was published in ''Science'' in 1996. It has been used to examine tissue-specific molecular changes and was employed in research associated with identification of the [[MEN1|MEN1 gene]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Emmert-Buck |first1=M. === Protein microarrays and signaling networks ===
Liotta and colleagues developed applications of reverse-phase protein array technology to measure proteins and phosphorylated signaling molecules in small clinical and research specimens. His 2001 study used reverse-phase microarrays to investigate signaling at the cancer invasion front. His other work also considered analytical challenges in [[Protein array|clinical protein arrays]]. With Rui Araujo, Liotta also published a mathematical study of the [[network topology]] required for robust perfect adaptation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Paweletz |first1=C. P. |last2=Charboneau |first2=L. |last3=Bichsel |first3=V. E. |last4=Simone |first4=N. L. |last5=Chen |first5=T. |last6=Gillespie |first6=J. W. |last7=Emmert-Buck |first7=M. R. |last8=Roth |first8=M. === Premalignant breast disease and autophagy ===
With Virginia Espina and colleagues, Liotta studied the survival of [[Precursor cells|malignant precursor cells]] in [[ductal carcinoma in situ]] (DCIS). His 2010 paper reported that autophagy supported survival of malignant precursor cells in their experimental model; a subsequent review discussed the biological behavior of DCIS.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Espina |first1=Virginia |last2=Mariani |first2=Brian D. |last3=Gallagher |first3=Rosa I. |last4=Tran |first4=Khoa |last5=Banks |first5=Stacey |last6=Wiedemann |first6=Joy |last7=Huryk |first7=Heather |last8=Mueller |first8=Claudius |last9=Adamo |first9=Luana |last10=Deng |first10=Jianghong |last11=Petricoin |first11=Emanuel F. |last12=Pastore |first12=Lucia |last13=Zaman |first13=Syed |last14=Menezes |first14=Geetha |last15=Mize |first15=James |date=2010-04-20 |title=Malignant precursor cells pre-exist in human breast DCIS and require autophagy for survival |journal=PLOS ONE |volume=5 |issue=4 |article-number=e10240 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0010240 |doi-access=free |issn=1932-6203 |pmc=2857649 |pmid=20421921 |bibcode=2010PLoSO...510240E }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Espina |first1=Virginia |last2=Liotta |first2=Lance A. |date=2011 |title=What is the malignant nature of human ductal carcinoma in situ? |journal=Nature Reviews. Cancer |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=68–75 |doi=10.1038/nrc2950 |issn=1474-1768 |pmc=3756606 |pmid=21150936}}</ref>
=== Nanoparticle biomarker ===
Working with Alessandra Luchini and other collaborators, Liotta investigated porous hydrogel particles for concentrating and protecting low-abundance biomolecules in biological samples. The group also developed 'protein painting', a technique for probing solvent-excluded regions at protein–protein interfaces. Related biomarker work examined urine lipoarabinomannan in tuberculosis.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Luchini |first1=Alessandra |last2=Geho |first2=David H. |last3=Bishop |first3=Barney |last4=Tran === Extracellular vesicles and mitophagy ===
His recent research with Marissa Howard examined extracellular vesicles in tumor interstitial fluid and their relationship to mitochondrial quality-control pathways. His 2022 paper described a secretory form of Parkin-independent [[mitophagy]] associated with [[Extracellular vesicle|extracellular vesicles]]. His 2025 study investigated secretory mitophagy under oxidative stress. <ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Howard |first1=Marissa |last2=Erickson |first2=James |last3=Cuba |first3=Zachary |last4=Kim |first4=Shawn |last5=Zhou |first5=Weidong |last6=Gade |first6=Purva |last7=Carter |first7=Rachel |last8=Mitchell |first8=Kelsey |last9=Branscome |first9=Heather |last10=Siddhi |first10=Daivik |last11=Alanazi |first11=Fatimah |last12=Kim |first12=Yuriy |last13=Araujo |first13=Robyn P. |last14=Haymond |first14=Amanda |last15=Luchini |first15=Alessandra |date=2022 |title=A secretory form of Parkin-independent mitophagy contributes to the repertoire of extracellular vesicles released into the tumour interstitial fluid in vivo |journal=Journal of Extracellular Vesicles |language=en |volume=11 |issue=7 |article-number=e12244 |doi=10.1002/jev2.12244 |doi-access=free |issn=2001-3078 |pmc=9314315 |pmid=35879267}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gade |first1=Purva V. |last2=Rivera |first2=Angela Victoria Rojas |last3=Hasanzadah |first3=Layla |last4=Strompf |first4=Sofie |last5=Philipson |first5=Thomas Raymond |last6=Gadziala |first6=Matthew |last7=Tyagi |first7=Atharva |last8=Bandam |first8=Arnav |last9=Gabbireddy |first9=Rithvik |last10=Kashanchi |first10=Fatah |last11=Haymond |first11=Amanda |last12=Liotta |first12=Lance A. |last13=Howard |first13=Marissa A. |date=2025-01-30 |title=Secretory mitophagy: an extracellular vesicle-mediated adaptive mechanism for cancer cell survival under oxidative stress |journal=Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology |volume=12 |article-number=1490902 |doi=10.3389/fcell.2024.1490902 |doi-access=free |issn=2296-634X |pmc=11821619 |pmid=39949610}}</ref>
